model_meta.description: Inferred concept model of a mechanical finger gripper that provides stable pinch and encompassing grasps through differential mechanical motion. Scope is limited to the core gripper grasp behavior and supported mechanical components; disclosed stopper/bias, flexion stopper, opposed-finger variants, and optional robot sensor/controller/positioning integration are intentionally outside scope. No item flows, ports, endpoints, directions, or interfaces are asserted because the available patent evidence does not establish a complete typed flow architecture. Flow and interface connectivity are outside this model's verification scope.

subsystems.description: Supports proximal finger pivot(s); optional palm surface stabilizes a load during an encompassing grasp.
First phalanx pivotally connected at its proximal end and second phalanx pivotally connected to the first phalanx distal end, with a load-contact surface.

Mechanism connected to the second phalanx; a disclosed configuration uses links forming essentially a parallelogram, while another uses a linear-motion link. These are alternative configurations, not asserted as simultaneous parts.
Single drive mechanism drives a corresponding actuation mechanism; specific drive technology is not fixed by this model.
External load contacted and grasped by the mechanical finger(s).

steps.description: Apply load at the stable pinch grasp region on the second phalanx contact surface.
Differential actuation permits the second phalanx to translate while its contact surface maintains a constant orientation.
Opposed fingers, when present, cooperate to pinch the object.
Apply load on the first phalanx or below the stable pinch region on the second phalanx.
Differential actuation permits the second phalanx to pivot.
The second phalanx pivots to perform an encompassing grasp; where the optional palm surface is present, it stabilizes the load.

requirements.statement: The gripper shall automatically perform a pinch grasp when load is applied within the stable pinch grasp region, allowing second-phalanx translation while maintaining contact-surface orientation.
The gripper shall automatically perform an encompassing grasp when load is applied on the first phalanx or below the stable pinch grasp region, allowing second-phalanx pivoting.
